---
title: "Maximum likelihood"
subtitle: "An unmodified optimizer, an encrypted objective"
---

```{python}
#| include: false
import os

os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "2")
```

Three sites count adverse events. None will share its counts, but all
want the joint maximum-likelihood estimate of the underlying rate.

The point of this example is what *doesn't* happen. SciPy's optimizer
is not modified, not wrapped in anything clever, and not told that
encryption is involved. It is handed an objective function; each time
it calls that function, three per-site log-likelihoods are encrypted,
summed homomorphically, and the total decrypted.

```{python}
from homomorphepy.examples import mle

fit = mle.run()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Markdown
lo, hi = fit.ci()
Markdown(f"""
| | value |
|---|---|
| site sizes | {fit.site_sizes} (n = {fit.n_total}) |
| **encrypted MLE** | **{fit.lambda_encrypted:.6f}** |
| pooled cleartext MLE | {fit.lambda_pooled:.6f} |
| difference | {fit.abs_difference:.2e} |
| standard error | {fit.std_error:.4f} |
| 95% CI | ({lo:.4f}, {hi:.4f}) |
| objective evaluations | {fit.n_objective_calls} |
""")
```

The encrypted estimate is `{python} f"{fit.lambda_encrypted:.6f}"`
against a pooled cleartext value of
`{python} f"{fit.lambda_pooled:.6f}"` — a difference of
`{python} f"{fit.abs_difference:.1e}"`.

Each of those `{python} fit.n_objective_calls` evaluations was a full
encrypt / homomorphic-sum / decrypt round.

## The comparison is exact, not another fit

For a Poisson rate the maximum-likelihood estimate is the sample mean
in closed form. The reference here is therefore the arithmetic mean of
the pooled counts, not a second numerical optimization — so the only
thing under test is the path through encryption.

## Where the standard error comes from

Not from the optimizer's internal curvature estimate. BFGS accumulates
an approximation to the inverse Hessian as a *search* device, and it
is well known to be an unreliable variance estimate. The SE reported
above is the analytic Fisher information for a Poisson rate,
$\sqrt{\hat\lambda/n}$.

```{python}
import math

analytic = math.sqrt(fit.lambda_encrypted / fit.n_total)
assert math.isclose(fit.std_error, analytic, rel_tol=1e-12)
```

## A caveat that is easy to state wrongly

A review of this port predicted that SciPy's default finite-difference
step (~1.5e-8) would fall below the CKKS noise floor and leave the
optimizer differentiating noise.

Measured, that does not happen at these parameters. The decrypted
objective is accurate to about 1e-13 on a value of magnitude 100, so
the implied gradient noise at the default step is ~1.7e-6 against a
true gradient of ~0.78 — five orders of margin. Both the default and
the widened step converge.

The step is nonetheless matched to R's `ndeps = 1e-3`, for
comparability rather than necessity. It becomes genuinely
load-bearing only when [differential privacy](dp.qmd) adds noise many
orders larger than CKKS's.
